stem: Which crop is usually propagated from vine cuttings?

options.content: Sweet potato
options.rationale: Correct: vine pieces about 30 cm long are planted on ridges.

options.content: Irish potato
options.rationale: Irish potatoes are grown from seed tubers.

options.content: Onion
options.rationale: Onions are grown from seed or small bulbs (sets).

options.content: Maize
options.rationale: Maize is grown from seed.

explanation: Sweet potatoes are planted from vine (stem) cuttings; roots form at buried nodes.

stem: What name is given to the pieces of sugar cane stem used for planting?

options.content: Setts
options.rationale: Correct: each sett has two or three nodes with buds.

options.content: Suckers
options.rationale: Suckers are shoots from the base of plants such as bananas.

options.content: Runners
options.rationale: Runners grow along the soil surface, as in strawberries.

options.content: Cloves
options.rationale: Cloves are the small bulbs of garlic.

explanation: Sugar cane is planted from setts laid in furrows.

stem: In budding and grafting, which tissues of the scion and the stock must be in close contact?

options.content: The pith of each stem
options.rationale: Pith does not divide to join the two parts.

options.content: The cambium layers
options.rationale: Correct: dividing cambium cells grow together to form the union.

options.content: The outer bark layers
options.rationale: Bark-to-bark contact does not make a union.

options.content: The epidermis and cuticle
options.rationale: These outer layers do not form the union.

explanation: The cambium of the scion must touch the cambium of the stock for the union to form.

stem: Which is an **advantage** of propagating oranges by budding rather than from seed?

options.content: The trees are free of all diseases of the parent
options.rationale: Budwood can carry the parent's diseases, especially viruses.

options.content: The trees show more variation for selection
options.rationale: Budding gives identical trees, not variation.

options.content: The trees are true to type and bear fruit sooner
options.rationale: Correct: budded trees are clones of a good variety and mature earlier.

options.content: Budding needs no skill or special tools
options.rationale: Budding needs skill and a sharp budding knife.

explanation: Vegetative propagation keeps the good qualities of the variety and shortens the time to bearing.

stem: Which statement about the offspring of asexual reproduction is correct?

options.content: They show more variation than offspring from seed
options.rationale: Variation comes from sexual reproduction.

options.content: They are genetically identical to the parent
options.rationale: Correct: they form a clone.

options.content: They always resist the diseases of the parent
options.rationale: They carry the same susceptibility as the parent.

options.content: They are produced by the fusion of two gametes
options.rationale: That describes sexual reproduction.

explanation: One parent, no fusion of gametes: the offspring are identical (a clone).

stem: A farmer plants sweet potato vines from an old field where the plants had small, crinkled, mottled leaves. Why is this unwise?

options.content: Cuttings from old fields always fail to form roots
options.rationale: Cuttings from healthy old plants root well; disease is the problem.

options.content: The new plants will show far too much variation to give an even crop
options.rationale: Cuttings produce identical plants, not variation.

options.content: Viruses in the parent vines pass into the new plants
options.rationale: Correct: vegetative material carries viruses.

options.content: Sweet potatoes can only be grown from seed
options.rationale: Sweet potatoes are normally grown from vine cuttings.

explanation: Diseases, especially viruses, are passed on in vegetative planting material; use clean vines.
hints: Mottled, crinkled leaves suggest a virus.

stem: Why are seed potatoes stored in diffuse light to form short green sprouts before planting?

options.content: Light kills most of the eyes, so that only one strong stem grows from each tuber
options.rationale: Light does not kill the eyes; it keeps the sprouts short and strong.

options.content: Green sprouts can be eaten safely before planting
options.rationale: Green parts of potatoes contain toxic substances and are not eaten.

options.content: Light turns the starch in the tuber into protein
options.rationale: Light does not convert starch into protein.

options.content: Short, sturdy sprouts give quick, even emergence
options.rationale: Correct: chitting speeds up establishment.

explanation: Chitting gives short, strong sprouts that grow away quickly and evenly.
hints: Compare short, strong sprouts with long, pale ones formed in the dark.

stem: All the bananas on a plantation came from suckers of one parent. A new disease arrives and attacks every plant. What explains this?

options.content: Plants grown from suckers are always weaker than seedlings, so they catch every disease
options.rationale: Suckers grow vigorously; the issue is identical genes.

options.content: Bananas lose their resistance when they flower
options.rationale: Flowering does not remove resistance.

options.content: The disease is spread only by suckers, not by other means
options.rationale: Diseases can spread in many ways; the uniform susceptibility is the key point.

options.content: They are a clone, so none of them has resistance
options.rationale: Correct: lack of variation is a risk of asexual reproduction.

explanation: Identical plants are equally susceptible, so a new disease can destroy a whole clonal crop.

stem: In grafting, the rootstock is the rooted plant onto which the scion is joined.
explanation: True. The scion provides the fruiting variety; the stock provides the roots.

stem: Vegetative planting material is lighter and easier to store than seed.
explanation: False. Tubers, cuttings and setts are bulky and perishable; seed is small, light and stores well.

stem: Match each crop with the planting material normally used.

right.content: Setts with two or three nodes

explanation: Each crop is multiplied from the vegetative part that carries buds.

stem: Complete the sentences about budding.

payload.template: A T-shaped cut is made in the bark of the {{blank:a}}. A single {{blank:b}} cut from the wanted variety is slipped under the bark so that its {{blank:c}} touches that of the stock.

explanation: T-budding joins a bud of the scion variety to the rootstock, cambium to cambium.

stem: Name the method of propagation in which a low branch is pegged into the soil to form roots while still attached to the parent.
explanation: **Layering**: the branch roots before it is cut from the parent.

stem: Seed potatoes of about 50 g each are planted at 90 cm × 30 cm on 0.2 ha. Calculate the mass of seed potatoes needed, in kg, to the nearest kg.
explanation: Area per plant = 0.9 × 0.3 = 0.27 m²; plants per ha = 10,000 ÷ 0.27 = 37,037; for 0.2 ha = 7,407 plants; mass = 7,407 × 50 g ÷ 1,000 = 370 kg.
workedSolution:
1. Area per plant = 0.90 × 0.30 = 0.27 m².
2. Plants per hectare = 10,000 ÷ 0.27 = 37,037.
3. Plants for 0.2 ha = 37,037 × 0.2 = 7,407.4.
4. Mass = 7,407.4 × 50 g = 370,370 g = 370 kg (to the nearest kg).
5. Using the per-hectare figure without multiplying by 0.2 gives 1852 kg, five times too much.
hints: Find plants per hectare from the spacing in metres.
Multiply by the area, then by the mass of one tuber.

stem: State **two** advantages and **two** disadvantages of asexual reproduction in crop production.

points.description: Advantage: offspring are true to type / identical to a good parent.
Advantage: faster maturity / earlier bearing (or: crops with little viable seed can be multiplied; rootstocks give resistance).
Disadvantage: diseases (especially viruses) pass to the offspring.
Disadvantage: no variation, so all are equally susceptible (or: bulky material that is hard to store and transport).

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Advantages: the new plants are identical to a good parent, and they mature or bear earlier. Disadvantages: viruses in the parent are passed on, and there is no variation, so a new disease can attack every plant.

explanation: Two of each, clearly labelled.
hints: Think about uniformity, speed, disease and storage.

stem: Describe how sugar cane is planted from setts.

points.description: Cut setts from healthy, disease-free mature cane.
Each sett has two or three nodes (buds).
Lay the setts end to end in furrows (horizontally) in moist soil.
Cover with soil; shoots grow from the buds and roots form at the nodes.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Healthy mature cane is cut into setts with two or three nodes each. The setts are laid flat, end to end, in furrows in moist soil and covered. Buds at the nodes grow into shoots and roots form at the nodes.

explanation: Material, preparation and planting.

stem: A farmer compares two ways of starting mango trees: (1) planting seeds from fruit bought at the market; (2) buying grafted trees of a named variety.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Which statement about trees from method (1) is correct?

options.content: The trees will be identical to the parent
options.rationale: Only vegetative propagation gives identical offspring.

options.content: The trees may vary and differ from the parent fruit
options.rationale: Correct: seedlings result from sexual reproduction.

options.content: The trees will bear fruit sooner than grafted trees
options.rationale: Seedlings usually take longer to bear.

options.content: The trees will carry all the parent's virus diseases

parts.explanation: Seedlings vary because of sexual reproduction.

points.description: Trees are true to type, so fruit quality of the named variety is known.
Trees bear fruit sooner.

Diseases in the scion can be passed on / all trees are equally susceptible to a new disease.

stem: Evaluate the use of asexual reproduction for producing Irish potatoes on a smallholding.

points.description: Seed tubers give plants identical to a good variety, so yield and quality are predictable.
Tubers contain stored food, so plants establish quickly and mature within one season.
Diseases, especially viruses, build up when farmers replant their own tubers year after year, lowering yields.
Seed tubers are bulky and expensive and need careful storage (diffuse light, cool, dry).
No variation, so a new disease or pest can affect the whole crop.
Judgement: asexual reproduction is the practical method, but certified disease-free seed should be bought regularly.

levels.descriptor: Accurate, well-developed explanation of several relevant points using correct agricultural terms, applied to the crop, animal or situation in the question, with a clear judgement where one is asked for.
Some relevant points explained, partly developed or only partly applied to the situation; any judgement is simple or one-sided.
Simple statements or a list of points with little explanation or application.

answerSpec.modelAnswer: Irish potatoes are propagated from seed tubers, so the crop is identical to the chosen variety and yields and quality are predictable. The stored food in the tuber means plants emerge and grow quickly, giving a crop within one season. However, seed tubers are bulky, a large mass is needed for each hectare, and they must be stored carefully. When a farmer replants his own tubers every year, viruses and other tuber-borne diseases build up and yields fall, and because all the plants are a clone a new disease can attack the whole crop. Overall, vegetative propagation is the practical method for potatoes, but the farmer should buy certified, disease-free seed potatoes every few seasons.

explanation: Balance the benefits against disease build-up and cost, then advise.
hints: Weigh true-to-type yields and speed against disease build-up and the cost of seed tubers.
